pathway.title: Mueller Water Products, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage and liquidity are the strongest support. Total debt is 1.34x reported EBITDA and net debt to reported EBITDA is negative 0.13x, or negative 0.09x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-07-28, while liquidity of USD 659.0 million is 1.46x the notes and the notes were quoted at 96.91% of principal at 2026-06-30. Because the facility is undrawn and the only bond falls due in June 2029, creditors face no scheduled call on liquidity until then. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation M2; calculation M3; calculation M23; calculation M24

Earnings have recovered on price rather than volume, so the gain is less durable than the margin suggests. Reported EBITDA rose 81.10% from USD 186.2 million in FY2023 to USD 337.2 million for the twelve months to 2026-06-30 on net sales growth of 15.96%, an incremental margin of 74.17%, and the 4.73% growth of nine months 2026 came from higher pricing with slightly lower volumes. The same operating leverage works in reverse: a return to FY2022 net sales would remove EBITDA at 69.51% of the lost sales. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M14; calculation M15; calculation M17; calculation M10

Guidance points to a softer fourth quarter, which tests how much of the third-quarter strength repeats. Fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of USD 367 million to USD 372 million implies USD 90.3 million to USD 95.3 million for the fourth quarter, 15.92% to 11.27% below the third quarter, although the fourth quarter of FY2025 was 6.25% above its third, and implied fourth-quarter net sales are 2.44% below to 0.18% above a year earlier. The third quarter included tariff refunds that the issuer calls non-recurring and does not quantify. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation M25; calculation M26; calculation M28; calculation M27

Demand is anchored in municipal replacement but concentrated in two customers, which is the main business risk. Municipal repair and replacement was 60% to 65% of FY2025 net sales on management's estimate and backlog was 6.02% higher at year-end, yet two customers bought 37% of FY2025 gross sales and owed 46.67% of net receivables, with no long-term contracts and competing products on their shelves, so a loss or repricing would hit sales, margin and collections together. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 127; calculation M9; calculation M10

Cash conversion is weakening, which limits how much of the earnings gain reaches creditors. Free cash flow was 43.42% of reported EBITDA in nine months 2026 against 78.99% in FY2024, because inventories absorbed USD 59.9 million and capital expenditures rose 32.93%, and it was 59.14% of adjusted net income against guidance of above 70%, which the issuer cut from above 85%. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-02-04_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation M5; calculation M30; calculation M29; calculation M13

Refinancing is a question of timing and intent rather than capacity. The facility matures on 2029-03-16, 91 days before the single note maturity, so the liquidity backstop ends first, but cash alone covers the notes 1.10x at 2026-06-30 before the dividend declared on 2026-07-28, and pro forma cash is not established, so the notes could be repaid from resources on hand if management keeps them rather than spend them on the unnamed transaction, capital expenditures and payouts. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M23

A repeat of the FY2022 earnings and cash drain would strain neither leverage nor liquidity. Reported EBITDA of USD 176.0 million in FY2022, 47.81% below the latest twelve months, would put total debt at 2.57x and cover the USD 18.0 million note coupon 9.78x, and the FY2022 fall in cash of USD 81.0 million would leave liquidity at USD 578.0 million, USD 128.0 million above the notes. The path is margin and cash erosion, not liquidity distress, unless debt-funded activity is added. Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_mwa-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 94–95; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M7; calculation M18; calculation M19; calculation M20; calculation M21; calculation M22; calculation M8

Governance and financial policy are creditor-neutral to supportive. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, dividends and repurchases took 43.67% of free cash flow in nine months 2026, and lender treatment has been orderly, but an unnamed transaction and the unsupplied debt documents leave event risk and legal capacity open. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M9

cells.text: Makes and markets valves, fire hydrants, pipe repair products, natural gas tapping and valve products, water metering systems, leak detection services and pressure management products for the transmission, distribution and measurement of water, mainly in the United States and Canada

Water Flow Solutions (iron gate, specialty and service brass valves) at USD 824.9 million, 57.70% of FY2025 net sales; Water Management Solutions (hydrants, repair, gas, metering, leak detection, pressure control) at USD 604.8 million, 42.30%
10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 126; calculation K1; calculation K2
Management estimate for FY2025 net sales: 60% to 65% municipal water repair and replacement, 25% to 30% residential construction, about 10% natural gas utilities and industrial

Sells mainly through waterworks distributors on non-exclusive terms and without long-term contracts; two customers were 20% and 17% of FY2025 gross sales; metering, leak detection and pressure products are also sold directly to municipalities
FY2025 net sales: United States 91.89%, Canada 5.43%, other 2.68%; manufacturing in the United States, Israel and China
10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 127; calculation K7; calculation K8; calculation K9

Management language: one of the largest installed bases of iron gate valves and fire hydrants in the United States and, in its words, the most recognized water infrastructure brand in the United States; the issuer says there are few competitors for most products, naming McWane and American Cast Iron Pipe Company for valves and hydrants and Sensus, Neptune, Badger Meter, Itron and Master Meter for meters
Purchased parts about 35% and raw materials such as brass ingot, scrap steel, sand and resin about 8% of FY2025 cost of sales; gross margin 36.14% in FY2025 and 38.24% in nine months 2026

Ten manufacturing facilities; iron foundries at Albertville and Chattanooga and a new brass foundry at Decatur; the Ariel, Israel plant makes Krausz repair products that bear most of the Section 232 tariff cost; 42% of the United States workforce is under collective agreements

Sales and operating income are lowest in the first and second fiscal quarters; backlog USD 320.7 million at 2025-09-30 against USD 302.5 million a year earlier, with about 22% of Water Flow Solutions backlog shipping after 2026
Municipal spending and residential construction cycles, distributor concentration, tariffs and inflation, product liability and environmental indemnities, and acquisition integration

rows.label: Liquidity: cash plus ABL excess availability

runs.text: Leverage is very low, which keeps debt service far from earnings. Total debt is 1.34x reported EBITDA and the annual coupon of USD 18.0 million is covered 18.73x, so earnings could fall by more than half before the coupon is threatened, and net debt is negative. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M2; calculation M8; calculation M18

Liquidity runs ahead of the only maturity. Liquidity of USD 659.0 million is 1.46x the USD 450.0 million of notes and nothing falls due until June 2029, so near-term market access does not decide the outcome. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation M4; calculation M23

Demand is anchored in municipal replacement. Repair and replacement is 60% to 65% of sales, utilities specify the products from a large installed base, and backlog of USD 320.7 million was 6.02% above a year earlier, which gives repeat demand with some visibility. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; calculation M10

Operating leverage has lifted earnings power. The EBITDA margin rose from 14.60% in FY2023 to 22.79% for the latest twelve months, so each dollar of sales now carries more cash toward debt service, provided pricing holds. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M16; calculation M14

Documented financial policy is creditor-aligned. No sponsor is named, dividends and repurchases were 43.67% of free cash flow in nine months 2026, no distribution was debt funded and the only waiver ended after 57 days, so extraction risk is low on behaviour. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M9

Two customers hold 37% of gross sales. They owed 46.67% of net receivables, have no long-term contracts and carry competing products, so a loss or repricing would hit volume, margin and collections together. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 127; calculation M9

The margin gain is price-led and partly non-recurring. An incremental margin of 74.17% on 15.96% sales growth, unquantified tariff refunds and a guidance-implied softer fourth quarter mean the earnings base could revert toward FY2022. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation M14; calculation M15; calculation M25

Cyclical, tariff and fixed-cost exposure amplifies any volume shortfall. Residential construction is 25% to 30% of sales, tariffs add about 3% of cost of sales and a significant portion of costs is fixed, so falling volumes cut EBITDA at 69.51% of lost sales. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 25–27; calculation M10; calculation M12; calculation M17

Cash conversion is falling while capital expenditures rise. Free cash flow was 43.42% of reported EBITDA in nine months 2026 against 78.99% in FY2024 and capital expenditures rose 32.93%, so less of each dollar of EBITDA reaches creditors or reserves. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M5; calculation M30

Refinancing is concentrated in one date and one open use of cash. The facility ends 91 days before the notes, and an unnamed transaction, capital expenditures and payouts compete for the cash that alone covers the notes 1.10x. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M23

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No acquisition, merger, divestiture, buyout or recapitalisation is described in any supplied document, and the cash flow statements show no acquisition spending from FY2023 to nine months 2026. The USD 450.0 million 4.0% senior notes due 2029-06-15 were issued on 2021-05-28 and, with cash on hand, redeemed the previous notes; they remain the only bond, are guaranteed by substantially all U.S. subsidiaries and rank behind borrowings under the USD 175.0 million asset-based facility, which was not drawn during the quarter ended 2026-06-30. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 5

The only transaction signal is an expense line. Portfolio optimization costs of USD 3.1 million in cost of sales and strategic reorganization charges of USD 18.9 million for nine months 2026 are described as including transaction-related expenses, leadership transition costs, an impairment and severance. No counterparty, nature, price, timing or funding is stated, so the transaction is not established, and up to USD 22.0 million of nine-month costs may relate to it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation K34

Two lender-side steps frame the creditor position. The December 2023 waiver capped ABL borrowings at USD 50.0 million until delayed reports were delivered and ended on 2024-02-06, and the amendment of 2024-03-28 extended the facility's maturity from 2025-07-29 to the earlier of 2029-03-28 and 91 days before the notes mature, and cut margins by about 50 bp. Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_mwa-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 116; calculation K41

A New Markets Tax Credit financing entered into on 2020-12-22 funded part of the Decatur foundry. The issuer expects the investor to exercise a put in December 2027 for nominal consideration, which would leave the issuer sole owner and give an estimated gain of USD 3.9 million, and it indemnifies the investor against recapture of the tax credits. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mueller Water is in a net cash position at 2026-06-30, with USD 495.3 million of cash against USD 452.9 million of carrying-value debt, so creditors face low leverage and no material maturity until June 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On reported EBITDA of USD 337.2 million for the twelve months to that date, total debt is 1.34x and net debt is negative 0.13x; net debt is negative USD 42.4 million, or negative USD 31.5 million pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-07-28. The issuer states only adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is calculated here, and cash interest paid is net of interest received.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has fallen because reported EBITDA grew while carrying-value debt stayed close to flat. Debt was USD 449.5 million at 2024-09-30 and USD 452.9 million at 2026-06-30, while reported EBITDA rose from USD 242.3 million in FY2024 to USD 307.7 million in FY2025 and USD 337.2 million for the twelve months to 2026-06-30. Total debt to reported EBITDA therefore fell from 1.86x to 1.47x and then 1.34x, and net debt to reported EBITDA fell from 0.58x to 0.07x and then negative 0.13x, as cash rose from USD 309.9 million to USD 431.5 million and then USD 495.3 million. On adjusted EBITDA of USD 368.5 million, built from the issuer's quarterly figures, the latest ratios are 1.23x and negative 0.12x, so reported EBITDA is the more conservative base. Pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-07-28, net debt to reported EBITDA is negative 0.09x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The capital structure is one USD 450.0 million 4.0% senior unsecured note due June 2029, guaranteed by substantially all U.S. subsidiaries and subordinate to an undrawn USD 175.0 million asset-based facility, plus small finance leases. Because 99.21% of scheduled principal falls in fiscal 2029, refinancing risk sits on one date, and the asset-based facility matures on 2029-03-16 while the notes remain outstanding, about three months earlier, so the liquidity backstop ends before the notes do. A refinancing therefore needs to be addressed before the facility expires, not only when the notes fall due.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The net cash position is thinner than it looks: counting only cash held outside Israel, Canada and China, net debt is USD 74.2 million, or 0.22x reported EBITDA, because USD 116.6 million of the cash is held abroad. Free cash flow conversion also fell to 43.42% in nine months 2026 from 78.99% in FY2024. The view would weaken if the unnamed transaction behind the transaction-related expenses were funded with debt, if distributions rose above free cash flow, or if conversion kept falling while capital expenditures stayed near USD 43.6 million for nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance for Mueller Water Products, Inc., as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway: the business, ownership, transaction, operating-model and governance facts that matter to creditors, drawn from the supplied filings and releases. It gives no instrument recommendation, peer ranking or recovery view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mueller Water names no sponsor or controlling shareholder in the supplied filings, and its financial policy returns modest cash to shareholders without debt funding, so governance adds little creditor risk beyond a concentrated distributor base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk is Low. Dividends and buybacks took 43.67% of free cash flow in nine months 2026, the only waiver the documents record lasted 57 days after a cyber incident, and the cash flow statements show no acquisition spending from FY2023 to nine months 2026. The unnamed transaction behind up to USD 22.0 million of nine-month charges and the unsupplied proxy statement are the open points.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership gives creditors no sponsor to extract value, but also no controlling holder to defend the company against a change of control. The filings name no sponsor or large holder, list 78 holders of record, and leave beneficial ownership to a proxy statement that is not supplied. The notes carry a put at 101% on a change of control only when a ratings decline accompanies it, and the indenture's definition of that decline is not supplied, so a takeover without it would leave noteholders with no put. The notes were rated Ba1 and BB+ at 2026-06-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns are modest and covered by free cash flow today, but in the weakest year they exceeded it. Dividends and repurchases were USD 48.3 million in nine months 2026, 43.67% of free cash flow of USD 110.6 million, against 33.08% in FY2025 and 26.07% in FY2024, and the quarterly dividend per share rose 4.48%. In FY2023 the outlay took 78.34% of free cash flow of USD 61.4 million, and in FY2022 free cash flow was negative USD 2.4 million against USD 71.5 million returned, met from cash; the next year only repurchases were cut, from USD 35.0 million to USD 10.0 million. No borrowing appears in the financing sections from FY2022 to nine months 2026, and USD 49.5 million of the USD 250.0 million repurchase authorization remains.

fields.value: Financial policy keeps debt flat while cash builds, which protects liquidity but commits to no deleveraging. Debt was USD 452.9 million and cash USD 495.3 million at 2026-06-30, against cash of USD 160.3 million at the end of FY2023. The notes have been redeemable at specified prices since 2024-06-15 and their principal is unchanged at USD 450.0 million; the issuer says only that liquidity may fund voluntary debt prepayments and repurchases based on excess cash flows, and that it may consider prepayment, refinancing or new debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: An unnamed transaction is the main open governance question. Up to USD 22.0 million of nine-month 2026 charges may relate to it, yet no document names the counterparty, direction, price or funding. The cash flow statements show no acquisition spending from FY2023 to nine months 2026, so there is no integration record to read, and management said in May 2026 that the balance sheet gives ample capacity for acquisitions. With cash above debt a cash-funded deal would leave leverage low, but a debt-funded one would not.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Lender treatment has been orderly. The December 2023 waiver capped ABL borrowings at USD 50.0 million until delayed reports were delivered after the October 2023 cyber incident and ended after 57 days; the amendment of 2024-03-28 then extended the facility from 2025-07-29 to 2029 and cut margins by about 50 bp. No exchange, priming or non-pro-rata transaction is stated in any supplied document. The facility now matures 91 days before the notes, so the liquidity line ends first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leadership has changed at the top within 343 days, but the chief executive succession is internal, which limits policy discontinuity. The chief financial officer started on 2025-03-03, the chief accounting officer on 2025-08-15 and the new chief executive on 2026-02-09, having been president and chief operating officer since May 2024; the chair is non-executive. Transition costs sit inside the strategic reorganization charges of USD 18.9 million for nine months 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is anchored by municipal repair demand but concentrated in two customers. They bought 37% of FY2025 gross sales and owed 46.67% of net receivables at 2025-09-30, and the business section puts the two largest distributors at the same combined 37%. Municipal repair and replacement drove 60% to 65% of FY2025 net sales on management's estimate, the installed base and utility specification support repeat demand, and backlog of USD 320.7 million was 6.02% above a year earlier. Yet the distributors hold no long-term contracts and also carry competing products, so a loss or repricing would hit sales, margin and collections together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins sit at a high that is partly non-recurring, so the earnings base behind payouts is less secure than the trend suggests. Gross margin rose from 29.75% in FY2023 to 36.14% in FY2025 and 38.24% in nine months 2026, and the Water Flow Solutions operating margin from 12.55% to 29.77%, on manufacturing efficiency, volume and pricing in FY2024 and on pricing and the closure of the legacy brass foundry in nine months 2026; the third quarter also included tariff refunds the issuer calls non-recurring and does not quantify. Inflation of about 4% and tariffs of about 3% of cost of sales continue, and capital expenditure guidance for FY2026 is 26.85% to 37.42% above FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a Low rating is that nothing in the supplied documents shows a structural barrier to a debt-funded transaction. No controlling holder is named, the direction of the unnamed transaction is not stated, and cash of USD 495.3 million plus USD 163.7 million of ABL availability could fund a deal without a new issue. The change-of-control put needs a ratings decline, and the indenture and credit agreement that set the baskets for payments, investments and added debt are not supplied, so what the documents permit is not established and the rating rests on documented behaviour. Customer concentration is the largest business risk, with two customers at 37% of gross sales. The view would worsen if the transaction proves debt funded or large against earnings, if a holder emerges with a stake that changes control, if payouts exceed free cash flow, or if a second waiver is needed. It would improve if the transaction is a small cash-funded disposal or bolt-on and the proxy statement shows dispersed ownership.

The USD 450.0 million 4.0% senior notes due 2029-06-15 were issued on 2021-05-28 and, with cash on hand, redeemed the previous notes; they remain the only bond, are guaranteed by substantially all U.S. subsidiaries and rank behind borrowings under the USD 175.0 million asset-based facility, which was not drawn during the quarter ended 2026-06-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Mueller Water Products, Inc., as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway: the overall credit profile, its strongest support, its weakest dimension and its primary downside, built from the supplied filings, releases and the three earlier module results. It gives no rating, security recommendation or portfolio sizing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mueller Water's fundamental credit profile is strong: total debt is 1.34x reported EBITDA and liquidity is 1.46x the notes, so creditors face little near-term default risk, while price-led margins, two customers at 37% of sales and one 2029 maturity are the constraints.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M2; calculation M23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA was USD 337.2 million for the twelve months to 2026-06-30, net debt is negative USD 42.4 million (negative USD 31.5 million pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-07-28) and liquidity is USD 659.0 million against USD 450.0 million of notes due 2029-06-15. A return to FY2022 earnings would lift total debt to 2.57x without threatening liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M1; calculation M3; calculation M4; calculation M19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage and liquidity are the strongest support. Total debt is 1.34x reported EBITDA and net debt to reported EBITDA is negative 0.13x, or negative 0.09x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-07-28, while liquidity of USD 659.0 million is 1.46x the notes and the notes were quoted at 96.91% of principal at 2026-06-30. Because the facility is undrawn and the only bond falls due in June 2029, creditors face no scheduled call on liquidity until then.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation M2; calculation M3; calculation M23; calculation M24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings have recovered on price rather than volume, so the gain is less durable than the margin suggests. Reported EBITDA rose 81.10% from USD 186.2 million in FY2023 to USD 337.2 million for the twelve months to 2026-06-30 on net sales growth of 15.96%, an incremental margin of 74.17%, and the 4.73% growth of nine months 2026 came from higher pricing with slightly lower volumes. The same operating leverage works in reverse: a return to FY2022 net sales would remove EBITDA at 69.51% of the lost sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M14; calculation M15; calculation M17; calculation M10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Guidance points to a softer fourth quarter, which tests how much of the third-quarter strength repeats. Fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of USD 367 million to USD 372 million implies USD 90.3 million to USD 95.3 million for the fourth quarter, 15.92% to 11.27% below the third quarter, although the fourth quarter of FY2025 was 6.25% above its third, and implied fourth-quarter net sales are 2.44% below to 0.18% above a year earlier. The third quarter included tariff refunds that the issuer calls non-recurring and does not quantify.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Demand is anchored in municipal replacement but concentrated in two customers, which is the main business risk. Municipal repair and replacement was 60% to 65% of FY2025 net sales on management's estimate and backlog was 6.02% higher at year-end, yet two customers bought 37% of FY2025 gross sales and owed 46.67% of net receivables, with no long-term contracts and competing products on their shelves, so a loss or repricing would hit sales, margin and collections together.

Free cash flow was 43.42% of reported EBITDA in nine months 2026 against 78.99% in FY2024, because inventories absorbed USD 59.9 million and capital expenditures rose 32.93%, and it was 59.14% of adjusted net income against guidance of above 70%, which the issuer cut from above 85%.

fields.value: Refinancing is a question of timing and intent rather than capacity. The facility matures on 2029-03-16, 91 days before the single note maturity, so the liquidity backstop ends first, but cash alone covers the notes 1.10x at 2026-06-30 before the dividend declared on 2026-07-28, and pro forma cash is not established, so the notes could be repaid from resources on hand if management keeps them rather than spend them on the unnamed transaction, capital expenditures and payouts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A repeat of the FY2022 earnings and cash drain would strain neither leverage nor liquidity. Reported EBITDA of USD 176.0 million in FY2022, 47.81% below the latest twelve months, would put total debt at 2.57x and cover the USD 18.0 million note coupon 9.78x, and the FY2022 fall in cash of USD 81.0 million would leave liquidity at USD 578.0 million, USD 128.0 million above the notes. The path is margin and cash erosion, not liquidity distress, unless debt-funded activity is added.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance and financial policy are creditor-neutral to supportive. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, dividends and repurchases took 43.67% of free cash flow in nine months 2026, and lender treatment has been orderly, but an unnamed transaction and the unsupplied debt documents leave event risk and legal capacity open.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against the strong view is that the earnings base is price-led and partly non-recurring: an incremental margin of 74.17% on 15.96% sales growth, unquantified third-quarter tariff refunds, guidance that implies a softer fourth quarter, and free cash flow at 59.14% of adjusted net income against guidance of above 70%. Concentration compounds it, since two customers at 37% of gross sales can reprice or leave together. The view survives because it rests on the balance sheet rather than margins: at FY2022 earnings total debt is still only 2.57x and liquidity stays USD 128.0 million above the notes. It would weaken if fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA lands below USD 90.3 million, if free cash flow stays below 70% of adjusted net income, if the unnamed transaction is debt funded, or if either large customer is lost. It would strengthen if the fourth quarter holds the third-quarter margin without refunds and cash is applied to the notes.

fields.value: Documented financial policy is creditor-aligned. No sponsor is named, dividends and repurchases were 43.67% of free cash flow in nine months 2026, no distribution was debt funded and the only waiver ended after 57 days, so extraction risk is low on behaviour.

fields.value: Two customers hold 37% of gross sales. They owed 46.67% of net receivables, have no long-term contracts and carry competing products, so a loss or repricing would hit volume, margin and collections together.

fields.value: The margin gain is price-led and partly non-recurring. An incremental margin of 74.17% on 15.96% sales growth, unquantified tariff refunds and a guidance-implied softer fourth quarter mean the earnings base could revert toward FY2022.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mueller Water makes the valves, hydrants, pipe repair products, gas products, metering systems and leak detection products that water utilities use to move and measure water in the United States and Canada, with FY2025 net sales of USD 1,429.7 million split 57.70% Water Flow Solutions and 42.30% Water Management Solutions. Municipal repair and replacement drives 60% to 65% of sales and utilities specify the products from a large installed base, so cash flow has more visibility than most industrial manufacturers; but 91.89% of sales are in the United States and two customers hold 37% of gross sales, so that visibility rests on one country and a few channel relationships. The seasonal pattern leaves the first half weakest, which is why the undrawn facility matters for liquidity preservation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation M10; calculation M9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor or controlling holder is named, so no owner can extract value or step in with support, and policy is set by the board: dividends and repurchases took 43.67% of free cash flow in nine months 2026 and none was debt funded. Substantially all U.S. subsidiaries borrow under the facility and guarantee the notes, which rank behind secured facility borrowings on U.S. inventory and receivables, and the put at 101% on a change of control applies only with a ratings decline whose definition is not supplied, so takeover protection for noteholders is thin; legal capacity for distributions and added debt is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; calculation M9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is predictable in its municipal core and cyclical at the edges. Water and sewerage rates rose 4.6% in the twelve months to 2025-09-30, which supports replacement budgets, while total housing starts fell 1.1% in FY2025 with single-family starts down 5.2%, and management expects a slowdown in new residential construction. Nine-month 2026 net sales grew 4.73% on pricing with slightly lower volumes, so pricing power is demonstrated but volume growth is not, and the backlog of USD 320.7 million, 6.02% above a year earlier, gives some visibility; pass-through works through price actions that the issuer says only mostly offset tariff costs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 56; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation M11; calculation M10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A significant portion of costs is fixed, so margins depend on volume and price. Purchased parts are about 35% and raw materials about 8% of cost of sales, tariffs add about 3% of cost of sales and inflation about 4%, and 42% of the United States workforce is under agreements expiring between December 2025 and October 2027. The EBITDA margin rose from 14.60% to 22.79% with a 74.17% incremental margin, and falling back to FY2022 sales would remove EBITDA at 69.51% of the lost sales, so margins can be defended only while pricing holds and volume does not fall far.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation M12; calculation M16; calculation M14; calculation M17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is moderate but rising and conversion of earnings into free cash flow is falling. Capital expenditures were up 32.93% in nine months 2026, are guided to USD 60 million to USD 65 million for FY2026 and were 17.23% of reported EBITDA for the latest twelve months, while free cash flow conversion fell from 78.99% in FY2024 to 55.90% in FY2025 and 43.42% in nine months 2026 as inventories absorbed USD 59.9 million. The filings do not split maintenance from growth spending, so flexibility to cut capital expenditures ahead of the 2029 maturity cannot be measured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; calculation M30; calculation M5; calculation M13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is moderate. The issuer says there are only a few competitors for most products and that end users are slow to change brands, which protects pricing, but most competitors are not publicly traded, so their behaviour cannot be monitored; the creditor implication is limited price-war risk with little visibility on it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of new entrants is low. Products must meet water works standards and be specified by utilities, and municipalities approve a limited number of hydrant brands, so entry is slow and margins are better protected than in an open market.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of substitutes is modest. No substitute for valves or hydrants is cited and the metering shift to electronic reading is expected to be slow, so revenue erosion from substitution is not a near-term credit driver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is high. Two customers buy 37% of gross sales without long-term contracts, carry competing products and are consolidating, which can intensify pricing pressure and makes revenue and receivables vulnerable to one commercial decision.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is moderate. Purchased parts are about 35% of cost of sales, outsourced production reduces control over delivery and cost, and the Israeli plant and imported components carry tariff exposure, so input shocks reach margin before they reach price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation M12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and regulatory factors are material through tariffs. U.S. tariffs on imported steel and aluminium rose from 25% to 50%, the Krausz repair products bear most of the cost, and tariffs add about 3% of cost of sales, which dilutes margin even where pricing offsets the dollar cost; the issuer also expects tariffs to raise demand for domestic product, which is an offsetting but unquantified benefit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Economic factors are material through interest rates, housing and municipal budgets. Rate-sensitive new residential construction is 25% to 30% of sales and municipal spending depends on local taxes and water rates, so a downturn in either reduces volumes. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths in credit terms are low leverage, USD 659.0 million of liquidity, municipal replacement demand from a large installed base, a margin that has risen to 22.79% on reported EBITDA and creditor-aligned policy, which together keep default risk low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M2; calculation M4; calculation M16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses are two customers at 37% of gross sales, price-led and partly non-recurring margins, falling cash conversion and a single 2029 maturity, which together limit how much of the earnings gain is secure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M9; calculation M5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the capacity and cost gains of the foundry programme, demand for domestic product under tariffs and use of cash to repay or refinance the notes ahead of 2029, which would remove the maturity concentration.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Threats that could weaken it are a debt-funded transaction, tariff escalation, a residential slowdown, distributor consolidation or loss, and labour agreements that expire between December 2025 and October 2027, each of which would cut volume or margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business dimensions are favourable but narrow. Scale and market position are Strong, with net sales of USD 1,479.3 million for the latest twelve months and products specified across the largest metropolitan areas, which absorbs shocks; competitive advantage is Strong because installed base and specification let the issuer raise prices with slightly lower volumes; business diversification is Average because 91.89% of sales are in the United States and two customers hold 37%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation M1; calculation M10; calculation M9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating dimensions are Average. Cost and capex flexibility is Average because a significant portion of costs is fixed and the capital expenditure plan rises, margin stability is Average because the 14.60% to 22.79% margin gain is price-led, and free cash flow stability is Average because conversion fell to 43.42% in nine months 2026 and free cash flow was negative USD 2.4 million in FY2022.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M16; calculation M5; calculation M21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial dimensions are Strong. Ability to refinance is Strong because total debt is 1.34x reported EBITDA and the notes were quoted at 96.91% of principal; liquidity is Strong at USD 659.0 million against USD 450.0 million of notes; financial policy and governance are Strong on documented behaviour, with legal capacity not established. The trend is improving on leverage and earnings and softening on cash conversion; the missing datapoints are the fiscal fourth quarter, customer terms and peer data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation M2; calculation M4; calculation M24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The short-term outlook over the next two years is steady earnings with softer momentum. Fiscal 2026 guidance is net sales of USD 1,470 million to USD 1,480 million and adjusted EBITDA of USD 367 million to USD 372 million, which supports leverage staying low, while the implied fourth quarter and the cut in free cash flow guidance show momentum fading. Tailwinds are water rates up 4.6%, aging infrastructure and a backlog 6.02% above a year earlier; headwinds are a residential slowdown, tariffs, inflation and municipal budget limits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57; calculation M13; calculation M11; calculation M25; calculation M10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The medium-term outlook over three to five years turns on pricing durability and the 2029 refinancing. Capacity investment in the iron foundries should lower unit cost and support output if demand holds, and the notes and facility mature in 2029, inside the horizon, so how cash is used between now and then decides whether refinancing is a formality or a risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a volume shortfall: slower residential construction and municipal deferral coincide with a distributor destocking or repricing, while tariffs and about 4% inflation keep costs rising. The first operational break is the price-cost spread, because fixed foundry and labour costs do not flex, and EBITDA then falls at about 69.51% of lost sales; FY2022 is the supplied precedent, with net sales 15.68% below the latest twelve months and EBITDA 47.81% below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_mwa-20240930.htm.jsonl, pages 94–95; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation M12; calculation M17; calculation M18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial transmission runs through working capital. In FY2022 inventories absorbed USD 98.3 million, free cash flow was negative USD 2.4 million and USD 71.5 million was still returned, so cash fell USD 81.0 million. Applied to today's debt, FY2022 EBITDA of USD 176.0 million gives total debt of 2.57x and covers the note coupon 9.78x, and a cash fall of that size leaves liquidity of USD 578.0 million, USD 128.0 million above the notes, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; this is a precedent-based illustration, not a default case.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_mwa-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 95; calculation M21; calculation M7; calculation M19; calculation M20; calculation M22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management levers are repurchases, which fell from USD 35.0 million to USD 10.0 million after FY2022, possible deferral of capital expenditures, whose flexibility cannot be measured, and the undrawn facility. The observable triggers are a guidance cut, backlog below USD 320.7 million and free cash flow below 70% of adjusted net income, and the scenario worsens materially only if the unnamed transaction adds debt or the facility is not extended before it ends 91 days ahead of the notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_mwa-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-K_2025-09-30_mwa-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mwa-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation M13; calculation M21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Mueller Water presents a strong business and financial profile supported by low leverage, USD 659.0 million of liquidity and entrenched municipal demand, but credit quality is constrained by price-led margins, two customers at 37% of gross sales and weakening cash conversion. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because municipal replacement anchors demand while earnings and cash conversion rest on pricing. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on whether cash is kept against the notes, which it covers 1.10x, and on extending the facility before 2029-03-16. The primary downside path is a price-led margin reversal with a customer loss and an inventory-driven cash drain, which at FY2022 earnings would leave total debt at 2.57x. Against typical leveraged credit issuers the financial profile looks stronger than the business profile, but that comparison is qualitative because no peer set is supplied. Further analysis would require the fiscal fourth quarter, customer terms, the executed debt documents and peer data. Fundamental credit completed with limitations. Top risk: reversal of price-led margins with two customers at 37% of sales.
